explanations: hashKey coerces to a signed 32-bit integer with h |= 0, so roughly half of all keys hash to a negative number. In JavaScript, % keeps the sign of the dividend, so shardFor returns a negative index, this.pools[negative] is undefined, and poolFor(...).query throws a TypeError for those restaurants. The result must be normalized, e.g. ((h % n) + n) % n or hashing with >>> 0.

Orders are routed by restaurant_id, so a customer's orders are spread across shards; the method scatters the query to every pool in parallel via Promise.all and merges. There is no customer-to-shard lookup, and the queries run concurrently, not sequentially.

Any order in the global top 20 is also in its own shard's top 20, so taking the per-shard top 20, merging, sorting descending, and slicing to 20 is correct. The sort compares b to a, which is descending, and correctness does not depend on single-shard placement.

Placement is hash mod shard count, so changing the count remaps most keys; no consistent hashing ring or assignment table exists, and reads go to the new shard where the old rows are not. The constructor only checks that the list is non-empty.
